statement: Natively trainable sparse/hybrid attention (co-designed with hardware-aligned kernels) is necessary for sparsity to yield real wall-clock speedup rather than theoretical FLOP reduction, but it requires from-scratch pretraining and does not retrofit off-the-shelf LLMs. NSA's hierarchical sparse attention with arithmetic-intensity-balanced kernels matches or beats full attention at 27B/3B MoE scale while delivering real speedup; NHA's intra-layer linear-RNN + sliding-window hybrid scales near-linearly and matches GSA operator speed, and can retrofit pretrained Transformers with lightweight fine-tuning (4 full-attention layers). The contrast: NSA needs from-scratch training for its full benefit, while NHA offers a retrofit path — but both show that without kernel-level co-design, sparse FLOP counts do not translate to latency gains.
